text:
alex: noticing a spike in missing spans for traces that go through the eu-exporter. logs show repeated TLS handshake failures to collector-eu.redwood-internal.net :eyes:

maria: can you paste the exact error from the exporter pod logs?

alex: sure, from exporter-0: `2026-03-14T10:02:11Z ERROR exporter_export: tls: handshake failure: remote error: bad certificate`

jeremy: that smells like cert rotation or CA bundle mismatch. Did we push the new certs to the sidecar image last week?

alex: we rotated leaf certs on 2026-03-13 via the cert-rotator job. sidecars were recycled but some exporter pods cached the old CA trust store? not sure.

maria: quick check — can anyone curl the collector endpoint from inside the exporter pod and show the cert chain?

alex: running inside exporter-0: `openssl s_client -connect collector-eu:4317 -showcerts`

alex: output (trimmed): `verify return:1
depth=0 CN = collector-eu.redwood-internal.net
subject=/CN=collector-eu.redwood-internal.net
issuer=/CN=internal-ca
Verify return code: 0 (ok)`

jeremy: weird, handshake still fails in app logs but openssl shows OK. Maybe mutual TLS required and exporter not presenting client cert. Did rotator also update client certs?

liz_ops: iirc we switched to mTLS for internal exporters 2 months ago. cert-rotator updated server CA only last job. client cert rotation might have failed for a subset of nodes. i can check cert-rotator run history.

sre-bot: incident created: T10021 - exporter-tls-handshake-eu - missing spans degradation - priority P1

maria: in the meantime can we flip routing to backup exporter in us-east for affected orgs? routing policy supports per-tenant fallback.

jeremy: yes, policy exists but need to be careful about GDPR cross-region. for a quick mitigation we can route non-sensitive telemetry to backup. i'll prepare a canary rule.

alex: adding a temporary denylist for collector-eu host in routing rules? or better: add explicit fallback route with low TTL.

maria: can someone check exporter health endpoints for client cert presence? `curl -s localhost:8888/metrics | grep cert` doesn't show client cert info. we should add a debug endpoint.

jeremy: pushing a small change to exporter sidecar to log cert subject on startup and expose `/debug/certs`. i'll canary to 1 pod.

alex: deployed to exporter-0-canary. logs show `client cert: CN=exporter-0.node.redwood-internal` for canary. non-canary still shows nothing.

liz_ops: found failed cert-rotator job on node pool gke-m-3 around 02:10Z on 2026-03-13 - it timed out. looks like ~30% of nodes didn't get client certs.

maria: OK root cause likely partial client cert roll. mitigation plan: 1) add fallback route for non-sensitive traffic 2) restart exporter pods on affected nodes 3) re-run cert-rotator with extended timeout 4) add cert presence metric and alert

jeremy: applied fallback route for traces to collector-us with respect to data residency flags (rolled out to 5% then 25%). deploy-bot: canary route applied. :rocket:

alex: restarted exporter pods on nodes gke-m-3-**. handshake errors drop to zero in restarted pods. missing spans rate falls from 8% -> 0.6% for those customers.

liz_ops: re-run cert-rotator completed successfully this time, client certs distributed. also created a post-deploy job to verify client cert presence.

maria: i've added a metric `exporter.client_cert_present` (gauge) and an alert `exporter_client_cert_drop` if gauge < 0.9 across the fleet for 5m.

jeremy: follow-ups: (1) add cert subject to startup logs for all sidecars (2) update rotation job to retry on timeout with exponential backoff (3) add a controlled fallback mechanism in routing UI so SRE can flip region fallback without code change

alex: creating incident follow-up ticket and assigning owners. thanks everyone.

liz_ops: small note for postmortem - telemetry retention spike occurred because fallback doubled ingest to us-east exporter for 30m. we should account for short-term retention and quota impacts in future runbooks.

maria: i'll draft a short postmortem and include recommended console UX change for one-click fallback and per-tenant GDPR flag visibility.

sre-bot: incident T10021 updated to resolved. postmortem assigned to maria and liz_ops.

alex: resolved for now, leaving this thread for the postmortem draft and any additional telemetry artifacts. :white_check_mark:
